current_date: August 2025 (cover: 'Planning Validation Checklist National and Local List of Requirements August 2025')
current_evidence: The council's 'Getting your application right first time' page links this PDF as 'Planning Validation Checklist 2025' (next to the superseded July 2023 version) and says the checklist was reviewed in summer 2025; a search found no 2026 version.

issues.detail: Grokbot dates the list 2025-07-01 from the URL slug 'july-2025'. The document's own cover is dated August 2025.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'Planning Validation Checklist National and Local List of Requirements August 2025'

issues.detail: All 7 tab_items (drawing and document standards) cite the superseded July 2023 checklist (media/4635/debvalidation-checklist-july-2023.pdf), not the current 2025 list. The tab content is therefore not sourced from the current document.
issues.evidence: The planning page lists both 'Planning Validation Checklist July 2023' and 'Planning Validation Checklist 2025'.

issues.detail: One tab item is advice and process text joined to navigation fragments, not a requirement: 'Fully annotated plans and drawings are more understandable ... [BACK TO CONTENTS PAGE] Page 4 Online planning applications Online planning applications are simple and easy to make using the Planning Portal'.
issues.evidence: Tab item 4 (from the 2023 PDF)

issues.detail: Householder is marked '(none)', but the Householder checklist requires a Tree Survey. It applies to development within 2 m of the canopy spread of a tree, or where trees on or next to the site (including street trees) could be affected.
issues.evidence: 3.1 Householder checklist: 'Application form, Location plan, Plans and Drawings, Correct fee, Tree Survey'; Tree Survey (p.42): 'Any proposals involving development within two metres of the canopy spread of a tree...'

issues.detail: Coastal Change Management Area Vulnerability Assessment is not captured. It is required for development in the Coastal Change Management Area (CCMA) and does not apply to householder applications.
issues.evidence: p.24: 'Development in the Coastal Change Management Area (CCMA)' / 'this does not apply to householder applications'

issues.detail:
Heritage Statement is missing under Full planning, Outline and Reserved matters, and Grokbot places it only under Advertisement consent. Its triggers are:
- Listed Building Consent applications
- major applications within, adjacent to or affecting conservation areas
- conservation area development, including demolition, that would materially affect appearance
- applications that may affect the significance of a heritage asset or its setting
- sites with potential archaeological interest
issues.evidence: Local list p.30: 'Listed Building Consent applications; Major planning applications within, adjacent or otherwise affecting conservation areas; ...'

issues.detail: Landscaping Principles is not captured. It applies to residential development of 150 or more new-build homes where public open space is provided, and of 11 to 149 homes on sites more than 2 km from a main park or Countryside Recreation Area where public open space is provided. Grokbot's 'Landscaping scheme / Landscape plan' row instead quotes an unrelated ecology line ('wildlife friendly landscaping scheme can be provided...').
issues.evidence: p.33: 'Residential development of 150 or more new build homes where public open space is being provided.'

issues.detail:
Design and Access Statement is not listed under Full planning, Outline or Reserved matters, although the 3.2 and 3.5 checklists include it. It applies to:
- 10 or more dwellings, or sites of 0.5 ha or more
- 1,000 sqm or more of new floorspace
- sites of 1 ha or more
- conservation area development of 1 or more dwellings, or a building or extension over 100 sqm
- Listed Building Consent
issues.evidence: pp.16-17 Design and Access Statement triggers; 3.2 checklist lists 'Design and Access Statement'

issues.detail: Outline and Reserved matters are both marked '(none)'. The source's 3.2 checklist covers 'Full or Reserved Matters', and the 3.5 Outline checklist carries the same conditional local items, including Affordable Housing, Air Quality, Flood Risk, SuDS, Transport, Tree Survey and Viability. All the local items Grokbot put under Full planning also apply to Outline and Reserved matters.
issues.evidence: Section 3.2 'Full or Reserved Matters' checklist; Section 3.5 'Outline Consent' lists the same conditional items

issues.detail: Listed building consent is marked '(none)', but the 3.3 Listed Building Consent checklist requires a Heritage Statement and a Design and Access Statement.
issues.evidence: 3.3 Listed Building Consent: 'Application form, Location plan, Plans and Drawings, Design and Access Statement, Heritage Statement'

issues.detail: Design and Access Statement and Heritage Statement are placed under Advertisement consent. The excerpt is the tail of the 3.3 Listed Building Consent checklist. The 3.4 Advertisement Consent checklist requires only the application form, location plan and an advertisement drawing at 1:20 or 1:50 showing size, position, materials, height, projection and any illumination.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'Design and Access Statement [guidance] Heritage Statement [guidance] [BACK TO CONTENTS PAGE] Page 9 ... 3.4 Advertisement Consent Validation Checklist'

issues.detail: Drainage Strategy / SuDS is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval' only because the trigger contains the words 'change of use', but that phrase is an exclusion. SuDS applies to all major development and to sites of 0.5 ha or more in Critical Drainage Areas, not to prior approvals. The 3.8 prior approval types simply refer to Planning Portal guidance.
issues.evidence: 'All major developments (except a change of use where no increase in permeable area is proposed)'

issues.detail: Lawful development cert is marked '(none)', but the 3.7 Lawful Use or Development checklist requires supporting evidence for an existing use. For a proposed development it requires elevations, a block plan, floor plans, a survey plan and a planning statement. Grokbot's 'Planning Statement' row under Full planning ('plan and a planning statement.') was actually taken from this LDC checklist.
issues.evidence: 3.7 Lawful Use or Development Validation Checklist Criteria

issues.detail: Works to trees is marked '(none)', but the 3.6 Tree Works checklist has specific requirements. For protected trees it requires a sketch plan, a specification of works, reasons and supporting evidence, and removal on grounds of condition needs a written report from a qualified arboricultural expert. Grokbot's Full planning 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment / Tree Survey' row quotes this tree-works text instead.
issues.evidence: Tree survey row excerpt: 'a qualified arboricultural expert ... If the applicant is alleging damage to property, then again reports are required...'

issues.detail: The trigger for 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment / Tree Survey' (Full planning) is garbled. It mixes tree-works text with the start of the 3.7 Lawful Use checklist. The real trigger is development within 2 m of the canopy spread of a tree, or trees on or adjacent to the site (including street trees) that may be affected.
issues.evidence: Tree Survey p.42; Grokbot excerpt ends '... 3.7 Lawful Use or Development Validation Checklist Criteria Application form...'

issues.detail:
The Retail / Town Centre trigger is cut off at 'Sequential Test 1.' It omits the actual tests:
- Sequential test: main town centre uses outside an existing centre that are not in accordance with an up-to-date plan
- Impact assessment: over 500 sqm outside Primary Shopping Areas or centres, over 300 sqm within 800 m of a district centre, and over 200 sqm within 800 m of a local centre
issues.evidence: Town Centre Uses (Sequential Test/Impact Assessment) section of the local list

issues.detail: The Viability Assessment trigger is cut off at 'Viability Appraisal Where or when this item is required: 1.' The real trigger covers all minor, other or major applications where on-site works or affordable housing are required by policy. It also covers cases where a policy financial contribution (off-site works, affordable housing or education) cannot be met.
issues.evidence: p.43: 'For all minor, other or major applications where on site works or affordable housing is required in accordance with adopted policy'

issues.detail: 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' reuses the town centre sequential test text ('Town Centre uses - Sequential Test/ Impact Assessment...'). It duplicates the retail row under a flood label. The list has no separate flood sequential or exception test item.
issues.evidence: Both rows have identical trigger_excerpt

issues.detail:
Several triggers are truncated:
- Air Quality stops at 'Leisure facil' and misses leisure or exhibition uses of 9,000 sqm or more, impacts on designated sites, and agricultural development posing a significant air-quality risk.
- Ecological Survey keeps only 'Where protected species are known to be present'. It misses likely significant effects on Ramsar sites, SPAs or SACs, sites within or adjacent to designated nature or geological sites, and Nature Improvement Areas.
issues.evidence: Air Quality Assessment and Ecological Survey and Report trigger lists in the local list
issues.grok_comment: The Ecological Survey trigger is indeed cut to "Where protected species are known to be present", but the workbook Air Quality trigger does include "Leisure facilities or exhibition centres of 9,000 m2 or more" and the designated-sites line; only the agricultural-development clause is lost.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The Air Quality trigger is mostly complete (only the agricultural clause lost). The Ecological Survey truncation stands.

issues.detail:
Several Full planning rows are built from explanatory or guidance text, not from list items:
- 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)' quotes the block plan description.
- 'Ventilation / Extraction details' and 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' quote the Noise Assessment's what-to-include guidance.
- 'Habitats Regulations Assessment information' is a fragment inside the Ecological Survey guidance.
- 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms' is a note that Heads of Terms 'may be required' during consideration.
issues.evidence: e.g. 'details of waste collection for example pubs/clubs where glass collection could be noisy.'

issues.detail: The trigger for 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' quotes the drawing-standards line on finished floor levels. The list actually requires sections where a proposal involves a change in levels or a sloping site, and for basement and attic conversions.
issues.evidence: Plans and Drawings: 'Sections - required where any proposal involves a change in levels or are on a sloping site'

issues.detail: About 20 rows carry 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. The source does name application types, in explicit per-type checklists (3.1 Householder, 3.2 Full or Reserved Matters, 3.3 LBC, 3.4 Adverts, 3.5 Outline, 3.6 Tree works, 3.7 LDC, 3.8 Other), so this inference was unnecessary. Examples include Affordable Housing Statement, Flood Risk Assessment, Transport Assessment and Viability Assessment.
issues.evidence: Section 3 'Validation Checklists for Each Application Type'

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Sefton list (dated August 2025 in the text, not July), but the tab items come from the superseded 2023 checklist. The app-type mapping ignores the source's explicit per-type checklists: Householder Tree Survey, Outline/RM/LBC/LDC/tree-works requirements and the CCMA, Heritage and Landscaping Principles items are missing, and several triggers are truncated or mislabelled.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
